scenes.02-why: Half of U.S. teens now use AI chatbots for schoolwork, and about four in ten use them for math. But language models are fluent, not exact, and a parent can't tell a confident wrong answer from a right one. So we asked: what if Alexa had to prove it?
scenes.03-homework: This is Show Your Work, on a simulated Alexa+ display. Maya solved 3x plus 5 equals 20 and got 25 over 3. Alexa doesn't guess. It sends her lines of work to our MCP server, which finds the exact step that changes the answer: x equals 5 satisfies line one, but not line two. An independent verifier replays that proof before Alexa says a word. Maya gets a hint, not the answer.
scenes.04-translation: The only AI step is turning words into equations, and the screen shows that translation back so a parent can check it. Everything after is exact rational arithmetic, with no floating point and no model in the loop.
scenes.05-typo: Some homework can't be right as written. Twenty tickets for three hundred dollars forces minus twelve child tickets, so the worksheet has a typo. That's a certified no, with a two-line proof.
scenes.06-forgery: Every card is an MCP App. Replay re-checks the proof live. Try a forgery changes one number and recomputes the hash, and the verifier still rejects it. A valid fingerprint can't make a false proof true.
scenes.07-memory: Alexa can make a practice problem whose answer key is verified before anyone sees it, and it remembers across sessions. The weekly report re-verifies every saved certificate before counting it, and names Maya's most common slip.
scenes.08-architecture: Under the hood: a self-hosted MCP server over Streamable HTTP, an interactive MCP Apps card that works in any compliant host, and a verifier that never imports the compiler. The same engine certifies research-level algebra too.
scenes.09-close: AI interprets. Compiler calculates. Verifier certifies.
